purpose: Static evidence for the Player object, its update path, and the correction of two false AI-decision-loop leads. This package is intended to guide retail ULUS10066 symbol transfer and overhaul hook recovery; addresses here are debug-prototype ELF virtual addresses unless stated otherwise.

evidence: Fight-player setup at 0x000859B4 allocates 0x2D0-byte objects and calls 0x000A01EC.
The one-player/special path calls it at 0x00085A98 with the literal 'Player 2'.
The multi-player path formats the literal 'Player %d' and calls it at 0x00085B58.
The constructor stores the class virtual-table/interface pointer 0x0057D03C at object+0x18 and creates multiple owned subobjects.
findings.implication: This is the strongest current static anchor for the in-fight Player/boxer simulation object.

evidence: Allocates an object-pointer array sized from owner+0x48.
Reads fight-session player selectors from the session area around +0x19B0/+0x19C0.
Creates each 0x2D0 Player object with 0x000A01EC and stores it in owner+0x24.
Called from three higher-level initialization paths at 0x0001EB54, 0x000B4C3C and 0x000C8B3C.
Reads player count from owner+0x48 and player-pointer array from owner+0x24.
For a single-player count returns the first entry; otherwise indexes the array by caller-supplied index.
Paired object teardown for the structure built by 0x000A01EC.
Walks and destroys the same owned subobjects created by the constructor.
Destroys the object stored at player+0x2BC by calling 0x00091D24 with deletion flag 3.

findings.correction: This function is not the AI decision-update loop.
evidence: Player constructor 0x000A01EC allocates exactly 0xD4 bytes, calls 0x00093C5C, then stores the resulting object at player+0x2BC.
The function formats the six known per-player AI modifier paths using the supplied player index and initializes a compact configuration/state object.
Its counterpart 0x00091D24 is called only from Player teardown for the same player+0x2BC object.

findings.correction: This function is not the AI decision-update loop.
evidence: Called from 0x000A0668 for player+0x2BC with deletion flag 3.
Reconstructs the same six ai/mods/p%d/... path strings from object+0xD0 before cleanup.
Optionally frees the 0xD4 object when the destructor flag requests it.
0x000A0894 is present in the Player virtual-table/interface block rooted at 0x0057D03C, in the virtual slot descriptor beginning at +0x28.
It operates directly on the 0x2D0 Player object created by 0x000A01EC.
It updates multiple countdown/state fields, evaluates collision/action predicates, modifies movement/action flags, drives owned subsystems, and invokes 0x000A1100.
The routine is large and stateful and has no direct JAL callers, consistent with virtual per-frame dispatch.
findings.implication: This replaces the previous ai/mod string consumers as the highest-value static entry point for tracing the actual in-fight Player update loop.

evidence: Called from Player::Update at 0x000A0FA0.
Also called from two punch/collision-region paths at 0x0002EB60 and 0x0002F14C, plus 0x0009D9BC.
Takes a Player pointer, a small event/action selector and a 16-bit code/value, then enters a very large branch/state calculation.
findings.implication: This is a strong candidate for the player/AI combat-convergence boundary and should be traced before unrelated subsystems.

next_static_steps: Trace callers/owners that invoke the Player virtual slot at +0x28 to recover the enclosing fight tick/update loop.
Trace 0x000A1100's callers and dominant callees to separate input/action events, hit resolution and damage/stun handling.
Find writes/consumers of Player fields modified by 0x000A0894 and 0x000A1100 that correlate with energy/health, stun, knockdown and attack state.
Transfer the recovered Player constructor/vtable/update signatures to retail ULUS10066 before declaring any executable hook safe.
